title: Second collection/task (stain-norm robustness or external-site eval)
context: After the first benchmark task is stable, M3 expands coverage by adding a second approved collection that tests either stain-normalization robustness (different staining protocols) or external-site generalization (held-out scanner/site not seen in training). This tests a realistic failure mode for pathology models and adds scientific value beyond in-distribution accuracy. The second collection must pass the full license gate + de-id re-scan before any derived artifact is produced. 100% provenance must be maintained. See PLAN.md (M3 Reproducibility & expansion, External-site / stain-normalization robustness evaluation).
objective: Identify, gate, ingest, and tile a second approved open collection — either for a stain-normalization robustness evaluation (different staining protocol) or an external-site generalization evaluation (held-out scanner/site). The collection must pass the sources/allowlist.yml license gate and the de-id re-scan before any derived artifact is produced. Publish results honestly (split ID, seeds, variance, preprocessing hash, compute provenance) showing either stain-normalization robustness or external-site generalization performance.
acceptanceCriteria: The second collection passes the full license gate: a new sources/allowlist.yml entry reaches status: approved before any ingest.
The de-id re-scan is run on the second collection (100% screened); any positive is quarantined; results reported.
100% provenance is maintained: every slide in the second collection has a manifest record with all required fields.
The evaluation adds either a stain-normalization robustness assessment or an external-site (held-out scanner/site) generalization evaluation.
Results are reported honestly with split ID, seeds, across-seed variance, preprocessing hash, and compute provenance.
A datasheet for the second dataset is produced and committed, carrying the 'not for clinical or diagnostic use; research only' notice.
Domain-reviewer and license-reviewer sign-off are recorded in the governance log.
output: A second approved collection ingested with full provenance + de-id re-scan, tiled, with an evaluation (stain-norm robustness or external-site generalization) and a datasheet, committed via PR.
